  1121: BUSTER_C_SHARED bool c_parse_builtin_type_layout(Target target, CTypeKind kind, u64* size_out, u32* alignment_out)
  1122: {
  1123:     TargetDataLayout layout = target_data_layout(target);
  1124:     u64 size = 0;
  1125:     u32 alignment = 0;
  1126:     switch (kind)
  1127:     {
  1128:     case C_TYPE_BOOL:
  1129:         size = layout.boolean.size;
  1130:         alignment = layout.boolean.alignment;
  1131:         break;
  1132:     case C_TYPE_CHAR:
  1133:         size = layout.plain_char.size;
  1134:         alignment = layout.plain_char.alignment;
  1135:         break;
  1136:     case C_TYPE_SIGNED_CHAR:
  1137:         size = layout.signed_char.size;
  1138:         alignment = layout.signed_char.alignment;
  1139:         break;
  1140:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_CHAR:
  1141:         size = layout.unsigned_char.size;
  1142:         alignment = layout.unsigned_char.alignment;
  1143:         break;
  1144:     case C_TYPE_SHORT:
  1145:         size = layout.short_integer.size;
  1146:         alignment = layout.short_integer.alignment;
  1147:         break;
  1148:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT:
  1149:         size = layout.unsigned_short_integer.size;
  1150:         alignment = layout.unsigned_short_integer.alignment;
  1151:         break;
  1152:     case C_TYPE_INT:
  1153:         size = layout.integer.size;
  1154:         alignment = layout.integer.alignment;
  1155:         break;
  1156:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT:
  1157:         size = layout.unsigned_integer.size;
  1158:         alignment = layout.unsigned_integer.alignment;
  1159:         break;
  1160:     case C_TYPE_FLOAT16:
  1161:     case C_TYPE_BFLOAT16:
  1162:     {
  1163:         TargetTypeLayout narrow = kind == C_TYPE_BFLOAT16 ? layout.bfloat16_type : layout.float16_type;
  1164:         size = narrow.size;
  1165:         alignment = narrow.alignment;
  1166:         break;
  1167:     }
  1168:     case C_TYPE_FLOAT:
  1169:         size = layout.float_type.size;
  1170:         alignment = layout.float_type.alignment;
  1171:         break;
  1172:     case C_TYPE_LONG:
  1173:         size = layout.long_integer.size;
  1174:         alignment = layout.long_integer.alignment;
  1175:         break;
  1176:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG:
  1177:         size = layout.unsigned_long_integer.size;
  1178:         alignment = layout.unsigned_long_integer.alignment;
  1179:         break;
  1180:     case C_TYPE_LONG_LONG:
  1181:         size = layout.long_long_integer.size;
  1182:         alignment = layout.long_long_integer.alignment;
  1183:         break;
  1184:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG:
  1185:         size = layout.unsigned_long_long_integer.size;
  1186:         alignment = layout.unsigned_long_long_integer.alignment;
  1187:         break;
  1188:     case C_TYPE_DOUBLE:
  1189:         size = layout.double_type.size;
  1190:         alignment = layout.double_type.alignment;
  1191:         break;
  1192:     case C_TYPE_NULLPTR:
  1193:     case C_TYPE_POINTER:
  1194:     case C_TYPE_FUNCTION:
  1195:         size = layout.pointer.size;
  1196:         alignment = layout.pointer.alignment;
  1197:         break;
  1198:     case C_TYPE_LONG_DOUBLE:
  1199:         size = layout.long_double_type.size;
  1200:         alignment = layout.long_double_type.alignment;
  1201:         break;
  1202:     // A complex value is two contiguous elements of its real type, so it is
  1203:     // twice as wide and no more strictly aligned. Clang agrees on all three
  1204:     // for every target here: sizeof/_Alignof are {8,4}, {16,8} and
  1205:     // {2*sizeof(long double), _Alignof(long double)}.
  1206:     case C_TYPE_FLOAT16_COMPLEX:
  1207:         size = layout.float16_type.size * 2;
  1208:         alignment = layout.float16_type.alignment;
  1209:         break;
  1210:     case C_TYPE_FLOAT_COMPLEX:
  1211:         size = layout.float_type.size * 2;
  1212:         alignment = layout.float_type.alignment;
  1213:         break;
  1214:     case C_TYPE_DOUBLE_COMPLEX:
  1215:         size = layout.double_type.size * 2;
  1216:         alignment = layout.double_type.alignment;
  1217:         break;
  1218:     case C_TYPE_LONG_DOUBLE_COMPLEX:
  1219:         size = layout.long_double_type.size * 2;
  1220:         alignment = layout.long_double_type.alignment;
  1221:         break;
  1222:     case C_TYPE_INT128:
  1223:         size = layout.integer128.size;
  1224:         alignment = layout.integer128.alignment;
  1225:         break;
  1226:     case C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_INT128:
  1227:         size = layout.unsigned_integer128.size;
  1228:         alignment = layout.unsigned_integer128.alignment;
  1229:         break;
  1230:     case C_TYPE_VA_LIST:
  1231:         size = layout.va_list.size;
  1232:         alignment = layout.va_list.alignment;
  1233:         break;
  1234:     // GNU gives `void` a size and an alignment of one so that arithmetic on a
  1235:     // `void *` steps by bytes; clang and gcc both fold `sizeof(void)`,
  1236:     // `sizeof(const void)` and `_Alignof(void)` to 1. It is an extension for
  1237:     // that arithmetic and for `sizeof`, never a licence to declare a `void`
  1238:     // object: every refusal of one keys on the *kind*, not on a zero size.
  1239:     case C_TYPE_VOID:
  1240:         size = 1;
  1241:         alignment = 1;
  1242:         break;
  1243:     case C_TYPE_ARRAY:
  1244:     case C_TYPE_VECTOR:
  1245:     case C_TYPE_STRUCT:
  1246:     case C_TYPE_UNION:
  1247:     case C_TYPE_ENUM:
  1248:     case C_TYPE_INVALID:
  1249:     case C_TYPE_COUNT:
  1250:         return false;
  1251:     }
  1252:     *size_out = size;
  1253:     *alignment_out = alignment;
  1254:     return true;
  1255: }
  1256:

  1258:    *constructing* a type rather than qualifying one: a value it could operate on

  1435:     // without walking the table.  A type a typedef gave an alignment of its own
  1436:     // is the one exception: its answer is not derivable from its kind, so it
  1437:     // falls through to the solve, where the alias branch reads the request.
  1438:     if (!any_type_alignment || !c_parse_type_alignment(result, requested))
  1439:     {
  1440:         CType requested_type = result->types[requested.value];
  1441:         u64 direct_size = 0;
  1442:         u32 direct_alignment = 0;
  1443:         if (c_parse_builtin_type_layout(preprocess.target, requested_type.kind, &direct_size, &direct_alignment))
  1444:         {
  1445:             if (direct_alignment)
  1446:             {
  1447:                 // The same promotion the seed below performs, on the one type
  1448:                 // this exit answers for; `_Atomic double` is the common shape
  1449:                 // and takes it unchanged, `_Atomic _Complex float` is the one
  1450:                 // that moves.
  1451:                 if (requested_type.is_atomic)
  1452:                 {
  1453:                     c_atomic_promoted_layout(target_data_layout(preprocess.target).atomic_max_width, &direct_size, &direct_alignment);
  1454:                 }
  1455:                 *size_out = direct_size;
  1456:                 *alignment_out = direct_alignment;
  1457:                 return true;
  1458:             }
  1459:         }
  1460:         else if (requested_type.kind == C_TYPE_ENUM && requested_type.element_type.value == C_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
  1461:         {
  1462:             *size_out = 4;
